description: Indicative South African retail benchmarks for materials not available as fixed-price, in-stock items in smart_house_products.json, plus conservative construction rates and cost shares. Retail and construction rates vary by supplier, location, scope and date; these are planning estimates, not supplier quotes.

windows.label: Aluminium windows (standard-size equivalent)
windows.averageMethod: Arithmetic mean of two in-stock 1200 x 1200 mm aluminium window listings (R1,219.99 and R1,299.00), normalized by their 1.44 m² reference area.

sources.name: K. Carrim
sources.priceLabel: R1,299.00; 1200 x 1200 mm bronze aluminium window

roofSheets.label: 0.47 mm IBR metal roof sheeting
roofSheets.averageMethod: Arithmetic mean of three South African listings for 0.47 mm, 4.8 m IBR sheets (R594.95, R469.90 and R479.00). Coverage uses a 686 mm effective cover width.

sources.name: Cashbuild
sources.priceLabel: R594.95; 0.47 mm x 4.8 m Aluzinc IBR

sources.name: PriceCheck (Buildit DTM listing)
sources.priceLabel: R469.90; 0.47 mm x 4.8 m Z150 IBR sheet

sources.name: Leroy Merlin South Africa
sources.priceLabel: R479.00; 0.47 mm x 4.8 m galvanized IBR roof sheet

roofTrusses.label: Timber roof truss structure
roofTrusses.averageMethod: Planning midpoint average of two published South African per-m² ranges: R250–R750 and R250–R650. Published ranges vary with spans, design and inclusions; this is a low-confidence structural benchmark, not a quote.

sources.name: Truss Master
sources.priceLabel: Published range: R250–R650 per m² for the timber structure

ceilingBoards.label: 6.4 mm gypsum ceiling board (1200 x 3000 mm)
ceilingBoards.averageMethod: Arithmetic mean of three 6.4 mm, 1200 x 3000 mm gypsum board listings: R245.15, R209.00 and R269.95.

sources.name: Builders South Africa
sources.priceLabel: R209.00 per Gyproc RhinoBoard 6.4 x 1200 x 3000 mm sheet

sources.name: Cashbuild
sources.priceLabel: R269.95 per 6.4 mm, 1200 x 3000 mm sheet

roofInsulation.label: 100 mm polyester roof insulation
roofInsulation.averageMethod: Arithmetic mean of two 100 mm polyester insulation rolls with 7.2 m² coverage, listed at R749.00 and R685.00.

basic.label: Low-cost single dwelling construction
basic.averageMethod: Published low-cost single-dwelling base rate for South Africa in 2026. It is a rough planning baseline; location, specification and actual scope vary.

sources.name: AprIQ
sources.priceLabel: R4,500/m² low-cost single dwelling base rate (South Africa, 2026)

standard.label: Standard house construction
standard.averageMethod: Published Gauteng-baseline naked construction rate for a standard single dwelling; materials, labour and specialist subcontractors are included, project add-ons are separate.

sources.name: AprIQ
sources.priceLabel: R9,400/m² standard single dwelling base rate (2025/26 Gauteng baseline)

premium.label: Luxury/premium house construction
premium.averageMethod: Published luxury-dwelling naked construction rate used as a conservative premium-finish proxy; finishes and location can raise actual costs.

sources.name: AprIQ
sources.priceLabel: R13,500/m² luxury dwelling base rate (2025/26 Gauteng baseline)

costShares.averageMethod: Use the lower end of published materials (55–60%) and labour (25–30%) shares within the base construction rate; the remaining 20% covers other direct services and specialist work. Add 10% professional fees (8% architect plus 2% structural-engineering reference) and 10% contingency, the lower end of a published 10–15% contingency range. The split is a planning model, not a quantity-surveyor bill.

sources.name: JobOS
sources.priceLabel: 2026 standard-build cost split: materials 55–60%, labour 25–30%, fees/compliance 8–12%, contingency 5–10%

sources.name: ooba Home Loans
sources.priceLabel: Labour 25–30%; architect up to 8%; structural engineer 2%; contingency guidance 10–15%

sources.name: AprIQ
sources.priceLabel: Standard base rate includes materials, labour and specialist subcontractors; contingency, fees and other project layers are added separately
